If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 1–2% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 1–2% in early-horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for bearish bias.  
When sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, shift forecast downward by 1–3% starting at day 10 to reflect sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1% in late-horizon (days 20–30) to prevent over-leverage.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, increase forecast slope by 0.5–1% in late-horizon to counteract sentiment-induced underestimation.  
If sentiment is positive but price is declining, add a 0.5–1% upward correction in mid-horizon to offset sentiment-driven overcorrection.
